content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to [company_name] and these forums. I received a [product_name] kit earlier this week. I've installed [product_name] [version_no] on my Dell laptop with Windows 10 but can't get the software to detect the PLC node. I disabled antivirus, tried both direct Ethernet and using a router, but no success. My computer also has [product_name] [version_no], which I use for another PLC. That version worked with my USB key and can detect the HMI, but not the PLC, regardless of my efforts. The HMI displays an error, DYN disconnected, with an IP address of 000.000.000.000. When selecting my PLC manually, the exact catalog number doesn't appear in the selection list. What am I missing? Why won't either [product_name] [version_no] or [version_no] detect the PLC node, but the HMI is visible? Any advice would be appreciated. Thank you, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. Your description is a bit confusing. There's no [product_name] [version_no] starter kit—these are two different product families. I suspect you have a [product_name] Starter Kit with TDE (order number [article_no]). For programming the [product_name], you need to install [product_name] software, which lets you create programs and message texts for the TDE. The TDE doesn't have its own programming environment. [product_name] [version_no] is only an add-on, intended for configuring basic panels, not for the TDE.

Thank you. Apologies for the confusion earlier. I have both types of PLCs, but my current question is about the [product_name]. I'll follow your recommendations and see if that helps. I did install the [product_name] software included in the kit, but it still didn't detect the PLC node. After disabling antivirus and connecting directly and via a hub, I had no luck. Are there any additional steps you suggest? I've tried both Windows 7 and Windows 10. Thanks again.
Please try this: Open [product_name] software and go to the "Network Project" tab. Click the "Go Online" button. After a few seconds, all available [product_name] basic modules should be visible.

Thanks for your help. Realizing I needed to use the [product_name] tool was the breakthrough. I received [product_name] [version_no] with my kit, but nowhere did it tell me to use the dedicated [product_name] software instead. Once installed and online as you explained, it detected the PLC successfully. Thank you so much. As an aside, if I connect a [version_no] PLC to my computer with [product_name] [version_no], can I go online and program it as well? Thanks again for your help. Sorry, I meant [product_name] software.

For programming, uploading programs, and live testing of the [product_name], you need [product_name] software. For programming and online activities with the [version_no], you need [product_name] [version_no]. The programming process for each is quite different.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced confusion about which programming software to use for different [company_name] PLCs, especially between two distinct product series. The main challenge was using the incorrect software to configure and program a PLC, coupled with unclear instructions in the kit. The absence of specific guidance delayed setup and complicated the learning process.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear, straightforward instructions specifying which software matches each PLC family from [company_name], and an easy setup process allowing the PLC to be found and programmed without confusion.
